classification.difficultyReason: Converts a volume ratio to a common linear factor, then uses the corresponding area factor.

content.prompt: A cylindrical container holds $125\text{ cm}^3$ of liquid when full, and requires $240\text{ cm}^2$ of material to manufacture. The company wants to increase the height and radius by the same enlargement factor to produce a cylindrical container that can hold $1000\text{ cm}^3$ of liquid. How much material will be required to produce the new container?

answer.short:
$960\text{ cm}^2$

The volume factor is $8$, so the length factor is $2$ and the material area factor is $4$.
answer.worked:
Let $k$ be the common enlargement factor for the height and radius.
$$\begin{align*}k^3&=\frac{1000}{125}\\k^3&=8\\k&=2\\A_{\text{new}}&=240\times2^2\\A_{\text{new}}&=960\text{ cm}^2\end{align*}$$
